title: First AA-AgentPerf-Local results for an NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X laptop
summary: An NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X laptop completes our local agent workload on Qwen3.8 27B in 18.7 minutes.
body:
# First AA-AgentPerf-Local results for an NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X laptop

NVIDIA’s RTX Spark N1X puts up to 128 GB of unified memory and a Blackwell GPU in a Windows laptop. In our first AA-AgentPerf-Local results, an RTX Spark laptop completes our local agent workload on Qwen3.8 27B in 18.7 minutes.

Laptops & workstations leaderboard AA-AgentPerf-Local on GitHub

This article shows AA-AgentPerf-Local results as of October 15, 2026 . Its charts update live, so they may differ from the figures in the text. For the latest results, see the laptops & workstations leaderboard .

## AA-AgentPerf-Local replays recorded agent sessions on local hardware

AA-AgentPerf-Local is our open-source tool for measuring how fast a laptop or workstation serves an AI agent. It replays recorded agent sessions against a model server running on the machine, with each request carrying the whole conversation so far, and measures how long the hardware takes to answer every turn.

The model generates exactly the number of tokens recorded for each turn, so every system does the same work. Most of each prompt is a repeat of the previous prompt’s contents. A server that keeps its cache only has to read the opening prompt of each task and what each turn adds (a median of about 450 tokens, and up to 6.4K after a large tool output).

## RTX Spark puts DGX Spark's chip in a Windows laptop

RTX Spark is NVIDIA’s platform for Windows on Arm PCs, which NVIDIA pitches as built to run AI agents locally. Its N1X chip is essentially the GB10 from DGX Spark (NVIDIA’s own recipe catalogue lists RTX Spark as GB10), with a 20-core Arm CPU, a 6,144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128 GB of LPDDR5X memory shared between them. In the laptop the memory runs faster, giving 10% more bandwidth than DGX Spark (300 GB/s against 273 GB/s). However, the chip runs at 45 to 80 W (NVIDIA’s stated range for N1X laptops), where GB10 is rated at 140 W.

We tested a prototype 15-inch Surface Laptop Ultra with 128 GB of memory, priced at 5,899.99. It runs Windows 11 on Arm and serves every model with a native Windows build of llama.cpp on the GPU. We ran it plugged in with Windows set to its high performance power mode.

## Each system runs its own recipe

We run each model with a recipe chosen for each system, using the vendor’s published recipe where one exists, so the runtime, speculative decoding and 4-bit weight format differ between systems. The RTX Spark laptop runs NVIDIA’s llama.cpp recipes for RTX Spark , ported into AA-AgentPerf-Local with NVIDIA’s settings.

Qwen3.8 27B Runtime Weights Speculative decoding

GeForce RTX 5090 desktop

The recipe behind each system’s fastest Qwen3.8 27B result

We are also testing more weight formats and runtimes, including smaller 4-bit formats such as IQ4_XS and Inco AI’s Splash , a Metal engine for Apple Silicon that uses DFlash speculative decoding. We will add their results once they pass our accuracy checks, which we will publish soon. Early tests show faster completion times on some systems.

## The RTX Spark laptop finishes the workload in 8-19 minutes, depending on the model

- ➤ On Qwen3.8 27B the RTX Spark laptop completes the workload in 18.7 minutes, close to DGX Spark (17.3), 2.0x faster than the MacBook Pro (37.6) and 1.8x faster than the Ryzen AI Halo (34.5). The GeForce RTX 5090 desktop is fastest, at 4.9 minutes.

- ➤ On Qwen3.6 35B A3B, which activates 3B parameters per token, it takes 7.6 minutes, close to DGX Spark (7.3), 1.5x faster than the Ryzen AI Halo (11.7) and 1.6x faster than the MacBook Pro (11.9).

- ➤ On Ling 3.0 Flash, the largest model on our leaderboard, it takes 15.3 minutes, close to DGX Spark (14.9) and 1.6x faster than the Ryzen AI Halo (25.1). Its 77 GB of weights do not fit on the MacBook Pro or the RTX 5090.

Total time the system takes to answer every turn of the workload's recorded agent tasks. Turns are sent one at a time, each with the conversation so far, and the model generates the same number of tokens as in the original recording, so every system does the same work. Time spent running tools is not included.

Qwen3.6 35B A3B, which activates 3B parameters per token, is the fastest model on every system, and the RTX Spark laptop finishes it in 7.6 minutes against 15.3 for Ling 3.0 Flash and 18.7 for the dense Qwen3.8 27B. The GeForce RTX 5090 desktop is the fastest system on every model that fits in its 32 GB.

### Completion Time | Qwen3.8 27B (Xhigh)

Prices for these systems are approximate and shift from week to week. At current prices, the 5,899.99 RTX Spark laptop costs more than the MacBook Pro (~3,700) and the Ryzen AI Halo (4,000) but slightly less than DGX Spark (~6,000), and the RTX 5090 desktop is the most expensive system at ~9,500 (a ~7,000 card plus a conservative 2,500 for the rest of the PC). The chart below uses these prices, and our leaderboard lets you enter your own.

### Reflection has released Beam, their first model launch

Reflection’s first model, Beam, scores 30 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it #2 among US open weights models

### First AA-AgentPerf results for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72

NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 serves up to ~5.7x the total throughput per megawatt of GB300 NVL72 on AA-AgentPerf, with first results on DeepSeek V4 Pro, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3.

### NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B A9B

Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now the leading US open weight model, scoring 26 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
